name: Philippines
sources: Department of Energy issuances|https://doe.gov.ph/;UP Law Center register (NARO)|https://naro.law.upd.edu.ph/;Lawphil|https://lawphil.net/
summary: Restructured under EPIRA, with the WESM spot market and retail competition. DOE circulars set policy and ERC resolutions give it binding effect, so most topics involve both. Requires access to ERC documents, which restricts automated requests, and OCR for scanned DOE files.

name: Thailand
english: Low (law-firm translations; binding texts in Thai)
summary: EGAT acts as single buyer; energy policy is set mainly through NEPC and EPAC resolutions rather than legislation. Several central instruments are still in draft (PDP2026, the Climate Change Bill, final direct PPA rules). Requires a Thai-reading reviewer and access to sources that restrict automated requests from outside Thailand.

name: Malaysia
summary: TNB is the single buyer in Peninsular Malaysia; Sabah and Sarawak have separate regulatory systems. Most rules are Energy Commission guidelines (rooftop solar, third-party access, tariffs) that are revised in place. Requires a method for recording guideline revisions and state-level law.

name: Singapore
summary: An unbundled market with private gas-fired generation; EMA is both regulator and system operator. Most rules are EMA codes, determinations and import licences rather than numbered acts. Its electricity-import licences correspond to export rules in Indonesia, Lao PDR and Cambodia.

name: Cambodia
english: Partial (the regulator posts official English versions of most regulations)
sources: Electricity Authority of Cambodia|https://eac.gov.kh/site/regulation?lang=en;Ministry of Mines and Energy|https://mme.gov.kh/
summary: EDC is the single buyer, regulated by the Electricity Authority of Cambodia. Rooftop solar rules have been revised almost annually, which allows comparison with Vietnam and Indonesia.

name: Lao PDR
summary: An export-oriented hydropower system in which EDL is the single buyer and there is no independent regulator yet. Best started once the amended Electricity Law (approved in principle in August 2026) is adopted. Requires a Lao-reading partner.

name: Brunei Darussalam
summary: Two vertically integrated utilities and a regulator established in 2017. A small number of rules, published in English; suited to a short country profile.

name: Timor-Leste
summary: ASEAN's newest member (admitted 26 October 2025). A largely diesel-based system, with a regulator established in 2020 and its first solar IPP under construction.

name: Myanmar
summary: Proposed as a watch list only: the framework law, tariffs and institutional changes, with each entry recording the issuing authority, given the disputed legitimacy of the government since 2021.
